source_components.:question/worked-solution:
The slope of $y=f(x)$ at $x=0$ is given by ${f}^{'}(0).$

We will calculate ${f}^{'}(x)$ using the chain rule. First, we express $f(x)$ as the composite function

$$
y=\operatorname{sin}u,\,u={x}^{2}+2x-1.
$$

Differentiating gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}=\operatorname{cos}u,\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=2x+2.
$$

We now apply the chain rule, and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{'}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} \\  & =\operatorname{cos}u\cdot (2x+2) \\  & =(2x+2)\operatorname{cos}u \\  & =(2x+2)\operatorname{cos}({x}^{2}+2x-1).\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluating at $x=0,$ we find

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{'}(0) & =(2\cdot 0+2)\operatorname{cos}({0}^{2}+2\cdot 0-1) \\  & =2\operatorname{cos}(-1) \\  & =2\operatorname{cos}1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of $y=f(x)$ at $x=0$ is $2\operatorname{cos}1.$

source_components.:question/problem: Find the equation of the tangent to the curve $y = \cos (5x-2 )$ at the point $\left(\dfrac 2 5,1\right).$
source_components.:question/worked-solution:
The slope of $y = f(x)$ at $x=\dfrac 2 5$ is given by $f'\left(\dfrac 2 5\right).$

We will calculate $f'(x)$ using the chain rule. First, we express $f(x)$ as the composite function

\[
y = \cos{u}, \qquad u = 5x-2.
\]

Differentiating gives

\[
\dfrac{\textrm d y}{\textrm d u} = -\sin u \qquad \style{font-family:inherit;}{\text{and}} \qquad \dfrac{\textrm d u}{\textrm d x} = 5.
\]

We now apply the chain rule, and get

\begin{align*}
f'(x) &= \dfrac{\textrm d y}{\textrm d u} \cdot \dfrac{\textrm d u}{\textrm d x}\\[5pt]
&=-\sin u \cdot 5\\[5pt]
&=-5\sin u\\[5pt]
&= -5\sin\left(5x-2 \right).
\end{align*}

Evaluating at $x=\dfrac 25,$ we find

\begin{eqnarray}
 \eqalign{

m=f'\left(\dfrac 25\right)  & =- 5 \sin \left(5\cdot \dfrac 2 5-2\right)\\[5pt] 
		& =- 5 \sin 0\\[5pt]
		&= 0.
 
       
    }
\end{eqnarray}
Finally, we find the equation of the tangent at the point $\left(\dfrac 2 5,1\right) \mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*}
y-y_1&=m(x-x_1)\\[5pt]
y-1&=0\left(x-\dfrac{2}{5}\right)\\[5pt]
y-1&=0\\[5pt]
y&=1.
\end{align*}

source_components.:question/problem: Find the equation of the tangent to the curve $f(x) = \cos{\left(x^3\right)}$ at the point $\left(0,1\right).$
source_components.:question/worked-solution:
First, the slope of $y = f(x)$ at $x = 0$ is given by $f'(0).$

We will calculate $f'(x)$ using the chain rule. First, we express $f(x)$ as the composite function

\[
y = \cos{u}, \qquad u = x^3.
\]

Differentiating gives

\[
\dfrac{\textrm d y}{\textrm d u} = -\sin{u}, \qquad \dfrac{\textrm d u}{\textrm d x} =3x^2.
\]

We now apply the chain rule, and get

\begin{align*}
\dfrac{\textrm d y}{\textrm d x} &= \dfrac{\textrm d y}{\textrm d u} \cdot \dfrac{\textrm d u}{\textrm d x}\\[5pt]

&= -\sin{u} \cdot 3x^2\\[5pt]

&=-3x^2\sin(x^3).
\end{align*}

Evaluating at $x=0,$ we find
\begin{align}
m=f'(0) & = -3(0)^2\sin(0^3) = 0.
\end{align}

Finally, we find the equation of the tangent at the point $(0,1) \mathbin{:}$
\begin{align}
y - y_1 & = m(x - x_1)\\[3pt]

y - 1 & = 0 \cdot \left(x - 0 \right)\\[3pt]

y - 1 & = 0\\[3pt]

y & =1.
\end{align}
